Nurul Amin, Senior Advocate instructed by Md Nurul Islam Chowdhury, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Appellants. 
Khandaker Mahbub Hossain, Senior Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Respondents.

Upazila Nirbahi Officer of Austagram and others ----- Appellants
Vs.

3. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, was that the Mosque and the Mazar situated in CS Plot No.1845 are known as Kutuber Masjid (hereinafter referred to as the Mosque) and Misir Fakir Mazar (hereinafter referred to as the Mazar). The Khadem of the Mosque residing in Plot No. 1845/1959 used to look after and conduct the day to day affairs of the Mosque and the Mazar. He died leaving behind three minor sons named Karon Ali, Museb Ali and Cherag Ali. They were enjoying the shirni and the gift offered to the Mosque and the Mazar. During the CS operation, the name of predecessor of the plaintiffs was recorded as Khademdar. In 1922, the Government of Bengal took over the Mosque and the Mazar under section 3 of the Ancient Monuments Preservation Act, 1904, in short, the Act VII of 1904 for preserving and, protecting it as the ancient monument. An agreement was executed between the Secretary of State and Salimunnessa Bibi, mother of the minor sons of Khadem on 6-3-1922. Since declaration of the Mosque as an ancient monument, the Archaeological Department of the Government had been preserving and protecting the Mosque and the Mazar situated on the suit land. One Sheikh Mannaf and others tried to grab the gifts offered by the people and cut away trees from the suit land. Then the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 1251 of 1934 in the Second Court of Munsif (now the Assistant Judge), Bajitpur for permanent injunction. The suit was decreed on 4-4-1935. While Museb Ali and Cherag Ali were in possession of the suit land, the record of rights (ROR) was not prepared correctly along with their names, but n it was also recorded in the names of Abdul Hakim and Nayeb Ali. Museb Ali filed Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 1972 in the 1st Court of Munsif (now the Assistant Judge), Bajitpur for correction of the ROR. The case was dismissed and on appeal vide Miscellaneous Appeal No. 202 of 1974, the miscellaneous case was allowed and the ROR was corrected in the names of Museb Ali and Cherag Ali. Thereafter, Cherag Ali died leaving behind plaintiff Nos. 2- 4 as the sons and they had been enjoying the shirnis and the gifts as Khademdar of the Mosque and the Mazar; the present record has been prepared in their names. The local. people did never form any committee for looking after the Mosque and the Mazar. In 1993, when the local people proposed to form a Managing Committee, plaintiff No. 3 wrote a letter to the Director, Archaeology, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, on 4-11-1993 requesting him to inform him whether any committee would be formed for the management of the Mosque and the Mazar and in reply to the said letter, the Director, Archaeology by his letter dated 18-12-1993 intimated to him that the appointment of the Imam of the Mosque and formation of a committee was not within their jurisdiction and they were willing to preserve and protect the ancient monuments only. Some local people tried to form a committee to look after the Mosque and the Mazar and to manage their day to day affairs. They managed to form a committee by defendant No.2 on 15-9-1994 and displaced the plaintiffs. They placed the proposed committee for approval before defendant No. 1 who without hearing the plaintiffs approved the same; hence the suit. 

 4. The suit was contested by defendant Nos. 2-4 and 6 by filing separate sets of written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint, contending, inter alia, that the Mosque and the Mazar were taken over by the then Government as the ancient monument. The plaintiffs had been using the lands as their personal property. The lands attached to the Mazar and the Mosque were not anybody's personal property. For looking after the Mosque and the Mazar, the Imam and the Moazzem were being appointed by the committee formed by the religious minded people and the committee was approved on 6-11-1994. The plaintiffs refused to work as the Khadem when asked by defendant Nos. 2-6. 

 "The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that it is well settled principle that in a case of affirmance, the revisional Court cannot interfere except in well defined circumstances such as misreading and non-consideration of material evidence on record. The High court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute without mentioning which evidence is misread or which evidence is non-considered. He next submits that the High Court Division exceeded its jurisdiction by making the Rule absolute without adverting to the findings of the courts below in dismissing the suit. He further submits that the plaintiffs prayed only for declaration that the Committee formed on 15-9-1994 vide memo No.502 by the defendant No.1 is illegal and inoperative and PW 1 stated in his evidence that আমি “১৫-৯=১৯৯৪ ইং তারিখের গঠিত ও ৬-১১-১৯৯৪ ইং তারিখের অনুমোদিত কমিটি বেআইনি ঘোষনার ডিক্রির আবেদন জানাইতেছি।” "But the High Court Division gave a direction that the plaintiffs are regulating the day to day affairs of the Mosque and Mazar without any interference of any other people or Government Office according to the law, which is beyond the pleadings and the Court cannot give any direction like this which is absolutely without jurisdiction." 

 9. Khandaker Mahbub Hossain, learned Counsel for the respondents, on the other hand, has supported the impugned judgment and order. He has further submitted that the plaintiffs predecessor acquired vested right in managing the affairs of the Mosque and the Mazar and enjoying the shirni selat offered therein as they were the Cheragi and the Khademdar thereof and their names were duly recorded in that capacity in the CS, the SA and the RS Khatians. Therefore, their right to manage the affairs of the Mazar and the Mosque and to enjoy the shirni selat offered therein by the devotees cannot be taken away in the name of forming a committee by the outsiders for running the day to day affairs of the Mazar and the Mosque. The High Court Division rightly interfered with the same. In support of his submission, Mr Hossain has referred to the judgments passed in the earlier litigations as mentioned while stating the case of the plaintiffs and the agreement dated 6-3-1922 entered into between the Secretary of State for India in Council and Salimunnessa Bibi, wife of the deceased Khadem and submitted that the appeal be dismissed. 

 20. Along with the report, the Photostat copy of the extract from the East Bengal and Asam Gazette notification dated 25th August, 1909 has been sent which shows that only the Mosque which is known as Kutub Mosque was declared as the ancient monument under section 3(1) of the Act VII of 1904 and accordingly, the Gazette was made and the same was being protected, maintained and preserved by the said Department. From the report, it further appears that the graveyard adjacent to the Mosque though were not mentioned in the gazette, is considered as part of the Mosque, but very near to the Mosque, new Mazar was being built/established (in Bangla, it has been stated as নতুন মাজার নির্মান করা হচ্ছে।”. In the report, it further has been stated that if new construction is made that will destroy the monumental beauty of the Mosque (in Bangla, it has been stated as "মসজিদের ঐতিহ্যগত নান্দনিক বৈশিষ্টকে ব্যাহত করবে।” and that will be against the provisions of the Antiquities Act, 1968. In the report, it has further been stated that letter was given from the regional office of the Director General to the Upazila Chairman, the Mosque committee (under challenge in the suit) and the Deputy Commissioner asking them to stop the new construction and also to evict the Madrasah established within the boundary. Along with the reports, the Director General of Archaeology also forwarded 3 (three) photographs of the views of the Mosque and the new constructions being made near to the Mosque, the copy of the two letters, one dated 30-3-2015 and the other dated 1-7-2012. The photographs show that new constructions are being made in the premises of the Mazar. By the letter dated 1-7-2001, the Regional Director of Archaeology requested the Deputy Commissioner, Kishoreganj to take step to remove the Madrasha built inside the boundary wall of the Mosque (in the letter, in Bangla, it has been stated as “কুতুব মসজিদের বেষ্টনী প্রাচীরের অভ্যন্তরে মসজিদ সংলগ্ন এলাকায় অবৈধভাবে গড়ে উঠা মাদ্রাসাটি”. The copy of the letter was given for information and necessary action to the Thana Nirbahi Officer, Austagram and the Chairman of the Masjid Committee (as at that time the masjid committee formed by the Thana Nirbahi Officer and approved by) Deputy Commissioner was in existence). The letter dated 30-3-2015 shows that the Regional Director, Archaeology by the said letter requested the Upazila Chairman, Austogram to give his opinion on the question of construction of 'গম্বুজ’ on the Mazar and under-construction of new 'গম্বুজ’ on the Mazar. In this letter, it was clearly stated that the Mosque in question was a protected ancient monument and any construction near the ancient monument was against the Antiquities Act, 1968. 

 21. As stated earlier, in fact, the plaintiffs filed the suit challenging the legality of the committee formed by the Upazila Nirbahi Officer and approved by the Deputy Commissioner for the management of the Mazar and the Mosque and running their day to day affairs. Their whole claim was that since prior to the CS khatian, their predecessor had been performing the job of Cheragi/Khadem of the Mosque and the Mazar in question and managing their day to day affairs and enjoying the shirni selat offered thereto and on the death of their predecessor, it is they who have been enjoying/appropriating the shirni selat offered to the Mazar and the Mosque by the devotees and their names were accordingly recorded in the CS khatian, the SA khatian and the RS khatian and by forming the committee challenged in the suit, they were being deprived of their said right. With the additional paper book filed on behalf of the plaintiff-respondents, the CS khatian, the SA khatian and the RS khatians have been incorporated. The CS khatian and the RS khatians have got presumptive value and in these two khatians, the name of Museb Ali, plaintiff No. 1 and the name of Cherag Ali, father of plaintiff Nos.2-4 were recorded as the Cheragi and Khademdar respectively, so the claim of the plaintiffs that they had been managing and running the day to day affairs of the Mosque and the Mazar and they had been enjoying the shirni selat offered by the devotees to the Mazar and the Mosque could not be disbelieved. That the plaintiffs had been managing and running the day to day affairs of the Mazar and the Mosque and that they had been enjoying/appropriating the shirni selat offered by the devotees are also apparent from the fact that in 1934, they filed a suit for permanent injunction against Sheikh Mannan, son of late Sheikh Katan Fakir and Sheikh Thandu who were creating disturbance in their enjoyment of shirni selat of the Mazar in question and the said suit ended on the basis of an award in favour of the plaintiffs. The judgment and decree of the said suit was filed in the trial Court and was proved and marked as exhibit-'3' The said award reads as follows: 

 23. It further appears that the suit land was wrongly recorded in the ROR khatian in the name of one Abdul Hakim and then Museb Ali Fakir (plaintiff No. 1) and Cherag Ali Fakir, predecessor-in-interest or plaintiff Nos. 2-4 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 1972 for correction of the record under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The case was dismissed against which the petitioners filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 202 of 1974 before the District Judge, Mymensingh and the appeal was allowed and the miscellaneous case was allowed and the name of the said Abdul Hakim was deleted and the record was corrected pursuant to the judgment passed in the miscellaneous appeal. All these facts prima facie show that it is the plaintiffs, who, in fact, had been managing the Mosque and the Mazar and running their day to day affairs and enjoying/appropriating the shirni selat offered therein. 

 24. It further appears that in support of the plaintiffs case that on 6-3-1922, an agreement was entered into between the Secretary of State of India in Council and Salimunnessa Bibi, mother of the minor sons of the Khadem for the protection of the Mosque filed the certified copy of the said agreement which was proved and marked as exhibit-'2'. And the recitals of this document and the terms embodied therein also clearly show that after the death of the Khadem, his widow Salimunnessa, looked after the Mosque and the Mazar on behalf of the minor sons, Karan Ali, Museb Ali and Cherag Ali. It further appears that the agreement was a registered one and since the original could not be filed, the plaintiffs called for the volume from the concerned Sub-Registrar's office and though the trial Court itself found that the volume proved the existence of the agreement, it did not rely upon it on the ground that since no evidence was produced about the execution of the deed, the genuineness thereof was not proved. This view of the trial Court was totally wrong inasmuch as it was simply impossible to produce evidence to prove its execution when the suit was heard. We are of the view that since the volume of the concerned agreement was called for from the concerned Sub-Registrar's office which clearly proved the existence of the deed of agreement, there was no scope of doubting its execution. The other reasons given by the trial Court not to rely upon the agreement dated 6-3-1922 were that it was a unilateral document and in the absence of the original, the same could not be accepted as a contract. It further appears that though the trial Court opined that the agreement could be accepted as angikarnama, (undertaking) it did not rely upon it on the ground that since the plaintiffs failed to file the original thereof and also failed to explain reason for their failure to file the original, the genuineness was not proved and that secondary evidence of a private document was admissible only when the party desirous of admitting it proved that the original was lost or destroyed being completely oblivious of the fact that the plaintiffs in order to prove the genuineness of the certified copy of the agreement called for the volume which proved the existence of the agreement. The Appellate Court while concurring with the said erroneous view of the trial Court unnecessarily wasted its time in entering into an elaborate discussion on section 90 of the Evidence Act completely overlooking the fact that the volume containing the agreement having been called for and the existence of the document having been proved, section 90 of the Evidence Act had no bearing on it. 

 27. From the judgment of the High Court Division, it appears that it made the Rule absolute on the finding that "In view of the above facts and circumstances the relevant points for disposal of the Revisional application is whether the learned lower Appellate Court failed to consider the material facts and law which resulted miscarriage of justice. It appears that the learned Trial Court without considering the plaint, written statement, exhibits and depositions of the PWs and DWs wrongly and illegally dismissed the suit. The lower Appellate Court also without considering the evidence on record and documents filed by both the parties wrongly and illegally dismissed the Appeal affirming the Judgment and decree of the Trial Court. In the absence of the law providing appointment and removal of Khadem of Mosque or Mazar the Khadem acting as such from the immemorial cannot be removed without findings of any fault. It also appears that the learned Trial Court went beyond his jurisdiction in giving direction to the defendants to form a new committee and the learned lower Appellate Court committed error of law occasioning failure of justice in affirming the judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court" 

 31. Now a question arises whether the management of the Mazar and the Mosque and their day to day affairs should be left exclusively in the hands of the plaintiffs or a Committee. We have tried to lay our hands on any law that governs the management of the Mazar and the Mosque and running their day to day affairs, so far we could not lay our hands to any such law. The learned Counsel for the respective party also failed to lay their hands on any such law. It appears that a law was promulgated in 1990 under the nomenclature “তপসিল ভূক্ত দরগা(পরিচালনা ও ব্যবস্থাপন) আইন, ১৯৯০, in short, the Ain, 1990 for the better management of the Dargahs and their properties. In the law, a তপসিল was appended mentioning as many as 201 Dargahs/Mazars, but the Mazar in question was not included therein. Subsequently, this law, ie the Ain, 1990, was repealed by the Act IX of 1994 and thereafter, no other law has been enacted, ie presently, there is no law regarding the management of the Mazar and the Mosque and to run their day to day affairs. From the report of the Director General of Archaeology as discussed above and the gazette, we have found that only the Mosque in question was declared as ancient monument, but the Mazar very much adjacent to it was not so declared and the Archaeological Department of the Government of Bangladesh is only protecting and preserving the same under the provisions of the Antiquities Act, 1968. In response to a letter issued by plaintiff No. 3, the Director, Archaeology clearly stated that they only protect and preserve the ancient monument and they were not authorized to form any committee. And the cause of action for the suit arose when the local people in league with the local administration, namely, Thana Nirbahi Officer formed a committee to run the day to day affairs of the Mosque and the Mazar in question as approved by the Deputy Commissioner, Kishoreganj. As discussed earlier, both the Courts below found that the Deputy Commissioner had no legal authority to form the committee for the management of the Mazar and the Mosque and run their day to day affairs. Mr Nurul Amin also failed to show any legal backing in forming the committee by the Thana Nirbahi Officer as approved by the Deputy Commissioner. Since there is no law to manage the Mazar or the Dargah and the Mosque and the further fact that the Department of Archaeology only protect and preserve the Mosque as an ancient monument, we have given our anxious consideration as to what the proper course for the smooth management and running of the day to day affairs thereof would be and we are of the view that there must be two separate committees for the Mosque and the Mazar for their proper management and running the day to day affairs preserving the right of the plaintiffs to enjoy and appropriate the shirni selat offered to the Mazar and the Mosque and to do this the only thing that is open to this Court is to invoke the power vested in this Court under article 104 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh for doing complete justice. 

 (f) The Thana Nirbahi Officer, Austogram is directed to form the two committees as stated in clauses (c) and (d) hereinbefore within 1 (one) month from the date of receipt of this judgment and in case any vacancy takes place in any of the two committees due to death or for physical disability, the Thana Nirbahi Officer shall fill up the vacancy in line with the mandate as stated in clauses (c) and (d). 

 (g)The Deputy Commissioner and the Thana Nirbahi Officer shall take immediate step to demolish all the new constructions including the Madrasah made in the Mazar premises and near the Mosque as stated in the report of the Director General, Archaeology (report has been quoted in the body of this judgment). It is further ordered that no new construction shall be made near the Mosque and the Mazar area. It is also ordered that henceforth, there shall be no new burial at the premises of the Mazar. The decree of the High Court Division stands modified accordingly.
